# Book III, Proposition 7

*Straight lines falling from a point on a diameter*

> If on the diameter of a circle a point be taken which is not the centre of the circle, and from the point straight lines fall upon the circle, that will be greatest on which the centre is, the remainder of the same diameter will be least, and of the rest the nearer to the straight line through the centre is always greater than the more remote, and only two equal straight lines will fall from the point on the circle, one on each side of the least straight line.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/07-idea.svg" alt="From a point on a diameter, not the centre, the straight line through the centre is greatest (red), the rest of the diameter least (yellow), and the others shrink as they turn, equal only in pairs (black, blue)." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>From a point on a diameter, not the centre, the straight line through the centre is greatest (red), the rest of the diameter least (yellow), and the others shrink as they turn, equal only in pairs (black, blue).</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/07.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition III.7, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABCD be a circle, and let AD be a diameter of it;

on AD let a point F be taken which is not the centre of the circle, let E be the centre of the circle,

and from F let straight lines FB, FC, FG fall upon the circle ABCD;

I say that FA is greatest, FD is least, and of the rest FB is greater than FC, and FC than FG.

For let BE, CE, GE be joined.

Then, since in any triangle two sides are greater than the remaining one, [I. 20]

EB, EF are greater than BF.

But AE is equal to BE;

therefore AF is greater than BF.

Again, since BE is equal to CE,

and FE is common,

the two sides BE, EF are equal to the two sides CE, EF.

But the angle BEF is also greater than the angle CEF;

therefore the base BF is greater than the base CF. [I. 24]

For the same reason

CF is also greater than FG.

Again, since GF, FE are greater than EG,

and EG is equal to ED,

GF, FE are greater than ED.

Let EF be subtracted from each;

therefore the remainder GF is greater than the remainder FD.

Therefore FA is greatest, FD is least, and FB is greater than FC, and FC than FG.

I say also that from the point F only two equal straight lines will fall on the circle ABCD, one on each side of the least FD.

For on the straight line EF, and at the point E on it, let the angle FEH be constructed equal to the angle GEF [I. 23], and let FH be joined.

Then, since GE is equal to EH,

and EF is common,

the two sides GE, EF are equal to the two sides HE, EF;

and the angle GEF is equal to the angle HEF;

therefore the base FG is equal to the base FH. [I. 4]

I say again that another straight line equal to FG will not fall on the circle from the point F.

For, if possible, let FK so fall.

Then, since FK is equal to FG, and FH to FG,

FK is also equal to FH,

the nearer to the straight line through the centre being thus equal to the more remote: which is impossible.

Therefore another straight line equal to GF will not fall from the point F upon the circle;

therefore only one straight line will so fall.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

## In Lean

✅ Proved

From [`Elements/BookIII/Prop07.lean`](../../Elements/BookIII/Prop07.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments, and our own notes are in `/- … -/`; the lines under each sentence are the Lean that carries it out.

```lean
/-- If on the diameter of a circle a point be taken which is not the centre of the circle, and from
the point straight lines fall upon the circle, that will be greatest on which the centre is, the
remainder of the same diameter will be least, and of the rest the nearer to the straight line
through the centre is always greater than the more remote, and only two equal straight lines
will fall from the point on the circle, one on each side of the least straight line. -/
theorem Prop7 {A D E F : Point} {ABCD : Circle} (hE : Centre E ABCD) (hA : OnCircle A ABCD)
    (hD : OnCircle D ABCD) (hAED : Between A E D) (hEFD : Between E F D) :
    (∀ B : Point, OnCircle B ABCD → B ≠ A → ‖F B‖ < ‖F A‖) ∧
    (∀ G : Point, OnCircle G ABCD → G ≠ D → ‖F D‖ < ‖F G‖) ∧
    (∀ B C : Point, OnCircle B ABCD → OnCircle C ABCD → SameSideOf B C A D →
      ∠ A F B < ∠ A F C → ‖F C‖ < ‖F B‖) ∧
    (∀ G : Point, OnCircle G ABCD → ¬ Collinear A D G → ∃ H : Point, OnCircle H ABCD ∧
      OppositeSidesOf H G A D ∧ ‖F H‖ = ‖F G‖ ∧
      ∀ K : Point, OnCircle K ABCD → ‖F K‖ = ‖F G‖ → K = G ∨ K = H) := by
  -- Let ABCD be a circle, and let AD be a diameter of it;
  have hAD : A ≠ D := ne_of_between_ends hAED
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hD_L⟩ := Postulate1 A D hAD
  have hE_L : OnLine E L := on_line_of_between_ends hAED hA_L hD_L
  -- on AD let a point F be taken which is not the centre of the circle, let E be the centre of
  -- the circle,
  have hF_L : OnLine F L := on_line_of_between_ends hEFD hE_L hD_L
  have hEF : E ≠ F := ne_of_between hEFD
  have hAEF : Between A E F := between_cut hAED hEFD
  have hFA : F ≠ A := (ne_of_between_ends hAEF).symm
  have hF_in : InsideCircle F ABCD :=
    inside_of_between (Or.inl (centre_inside hE)) (Or.inr hD) hEFD
  /- A point of the circle on the diameter is A or D (System E, Circle 1). -/
  have hends : ∀ K, OnCircle K ABCD → OnLine K L → K ≠ A → K = D := by
    intro K hK hK_L hKA
    have hAEK : Between A E K :=
      between_of_inside_chord hE_L hA_L hK_L (centre_inside hE) hA hK hKA.symm
    exact (OnRay.of_between_between hAED hAEK).eq_of_len_eq (Definition15 hE hK hD)
  /- FD is less than FA, for FD is less than ED, which is equal to EA, and EA is less
     than FA. -/
  have hDA : ‖F D‖ < ‖F A‖ := by
    have h₁ : ‖D F‖ < ‖D E‖ := len_lt_of_between (between_symm hEFD)
    have h₂ : ‖A E‖ < ‖A F‖ := len_lt_of_between hAEF
    rw [len_symm D F, len_symm D E, Definition15 hE hD hA, len_symm E A] at h₁
    rw [len_symm A F] at h₂
    exact lt_trans h₁ h₂
  -- and from F let straight lines FB, FC, FG fall upon the circle ABCD;
  -- I say that FA is greatest, FD is least, and of the rest FB is greater than FC, and FC than
  -- FG.
  -- For let BE, CE, GE be joined.
  have hgreatest : ∀ B : Point, OnCircle B ABCD → B ≠ A → ‖F B‖ < ‖F A‖ := by
    intro B hB hBA
    by_cases hB_L : OnLine B L
    · rw [hends B hB hB_L hBA]
      exact hDA
    have hEBF : Triangle E B F := (Triangle.of_line hE_L hF_L hEF hB_L).acb
    -- Then, since in any triangle two sides are greater than the remaining one, [I. 20]
    -- EB, EF are greater than BF.
    have h20 : ‖B F‖ < ‖B E‖ + ‖E F‖ := (BookI.Prop20 hEBF).1
    -- But AE is equal to BE;
    have hAE : ‖A E‖ = ‖B E‖ := by rw [len_symm A E, len_symm B E]; exact Definition15 hE hA hB
    -- therefore AF is greater than BF.
    rw [← hAE, len_add_of_between hAEF, len_symm B F, len_symm A F] at h20
    exact h20
  have hnearer : ∀ B C : Point, OnCircle B ABCD → OnCircle C ABCD → SameSideOf B C A D →
      ∠ A F B < ∠ A F C → ‖F C‖ < ‖F B‖ := by
    intro B C hB hC hBC hlt
    -- Again, since BE is equal to CE,
    have hBE : ‖E B‖ = ‖E C‖ := Definition15 hE hB hC
    -- and FE is common,
    have hEF_common : ‖E F‖ = ‖E F‖ := rfl
    -- the two sides BE, EF are equal to the two sides CE, EF.
    -- But the angle BEF is also greater than the angle CEF;
    have hBC' : SameSideOf B C F E := SameSideOf.of_line hEF.symm hF_L hE_L (hBC.sameSide hA_L hD_L)
    have hBF : B ≠ F := fun e => inside_not_on hF_in (e ▸ hB)
    have hCF : C ≠ F := fun e => inside_not_on hF_in (e ▸ hC)
    /- Euclid reads this off the figure, the gap Augustus De Morgan points out (Heath,
       vol. 2, p. 15). The angle EFB is the angle AFB, since E is on FA, so FB falls within
       the angle EFC (`BookI.Prop24.within`) and crosses EC at a point M (`crossbar`). -/
    have hEray : OnRay E F A := OnRay.of_between (between_symm hAEF)
    rw [← angle_onRay_left hEray hBF, ← angle_onRay_left hEray hCF] at hlt
    have hwithin : SameSideOf B E F C := BookI.Prop24.within hBC'.symm hlt
    obtain ⟨M, hEMC, hM⟩ := crossbar hBC' hwithin
    have hM_in : InsideCircle M ABCD := inside_of_between (Or.inl (centre_inside hE)) (Or.inr hC) hEMC
    /- M is between F and B: it is on the ray from F through B, and not beyond B, for
       then B would be within the circle (System E, Circle 2). -/
    have hFMB : Between F M B := by
      obtain ⟨-, hMF, ⟨N, hF_N, hB_N, hM_N⟩, hMFB⟩ := hM
      have hMB : M ≠ B := fun e => inside_not_on hM_in (e ▸ hB)
      rcases between_cases hMF.symm hMB hBF.symm hF_N hM_N hB_N with h | h | h
      · exact h
      · exact absurd h hMFB
      · exact absurd hB (inside_not_on (inside_of_between (Or.inl hF_in) (Or.inl hM_in) h))
    have hBFE : Triangle B F E := hBC'.triangle.cab
    have hang : ∠ C E F < ∠ B E F := by
      rw [← angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hEMC) hEF.symm]
      exact angle_lt_of_between hBFE (between_symm hFMB)
    -- therefore the base BF is greater than the base CF. [I. 24]
    have hECF : Triangle E C F := hBC'.symm.triangle.bca
    have h24 : ‖C F‖ < ‖B F‖ := BookI.Prop24 hBFE.cab hECF hBE hEF_common hang
    rw [len_symm C F, len_symm B F] at h24
    exact h24
  -- For the same reason
  -- CF is also greater than FG.
  /- The Lean above was said of any two points B, C on one side of AD, and C, G are
     such a pair. -/
  have hleast : ∀ G : Point, OnCircle G ABCD → G ≠ D → ‖F D‖ < ‖F G‖ := by
    intro G hG hGD
    by_cases hG_L : OnLine G L
    · have hGA : G = A := Classical.byContradiction fun h => hGD (hends G hG hG_L h)
      rw [hGA]
      exact hDA
    have hFGE : Triangle F G E := (Triangle.of_line hF_L hE_L hEF.symm hG_L).acb
    -- Again, since GF, FE are greater than EG,
    have h20 : ‖G E‖ < ‖G F‖ + ‖F E‖ := (BookI.Prop20 hFGE).1
    -- and EG is equal to ED,
    have hEG : ‖E G‖ = ‖E D‖ := Definition15 hE hG hD
    -- GF, FE are greater than ED.
    rw [len_symm G E, hEG] at h20
    -- Let EF be subtracted from each;
    -- therefore the remainder GF is greater than the remainder FD.
    rw [← len_add_of_between hEFD, len_symm F E, add_comm (‖G F‖)] at h20
    rw [len_symm F G]
    exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left h20
  -- Therefore FA is greatest, FD is least, and FB is greater than FC, and FC than FG.
  refine ⟨hgreatest, hleast, hnearer, ?_⟩
  -- I say also that from the point F only two equal straight lines will fall on the circle
  -- ABCD, one on each side of the least FD.
  intro G hG hG_AD
  have hG_L : ¬ OnLine G L := fun h => hG_AD ⟨L, hA_L, hD_L, h⟩
  -- For on the straight line EF, and at the point E on it, let the angle FEH be constructed
  -- equal to the angle GEF [I. 23], and let FH be joined.
  have hEFG : Triangle E F G := Triangle.of_line hE_L hF_L hEF hG_L
  obtain ⟨P, hPG, -⟩ := exists_point_opposite_side hG_L []
  have hP_EF : ¬ Collinear E F P := Triangle.of_line hE_L hF_L hEF hPG.1
  obtain ⟨H', F', hF', hH', hang⟩ := BookI.Prop23 hEF hEFG.cab hP_EF
  have hEH' : E ≠ H' := hH'.triangle.ne₁₃
  /- H is where the straight line EH' meets the circle on the side of E where H' is
     (System E, Intersections 5, with H'E produced to a point Q). -/
  obtain ⟨N, hE_N, hH'_N⟩ := Postulate1 E H' hEH'
  obtain ⟨Q, hH'EQ⟩ := produce hEH'.symm
  have hQ_N : OnLine Q N := on_line_of_between hH'EQ hH'_N hE_N
  obtain ⟨H, hH, -, hHEQ⟩ :=
    line_circle_beyond (centre_inside hE) hE_N hQ_N (ne_of_between (between_symm hH'EQ))
  have hH_ray : OnRay H E H' := OnRay.of_between_between (between_symm hH'EQ) (between_symm hHEQ)
  /- H is on the other side of AD from G. -/
  have hHP : SameSideOf H P E F := SameSideOf.of_onRay hH_ray hH'
  have hHG_EF : OppositeSidesOf H G E F :=
    hHP.trans_opposite (OppositeSidesOf.of_line hEF hE_L hF_L hPG)
  have hHG : OppositeSidesOf H G A D :=
    OppositeSidesOf.of_line hAD hA_L hD_L (hHG_EF.oppositeSides hE_L hF_L)
  -- Then, since GE is equal to EH,
  have hEH : ‖E H‖ = ‖E G‖ := Definition15 hE hH hG
  -- and EF is common,
  have hEF_common : ‖E F‖ = ‖E F‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides GE, EF are equal to the two sides HE, EF;
  -- and the angle GEF is equal to the angle HEF;
  have hFEH : ∠ F E H = ∠ G E F :=
    (angle_eq_of_onRay hF'.symm hH_ray).trans ((angle_symm hF'.2.1 hEH'.symm).trans hang)
  have hEHF : Triangle E H F := hHG_EF.triangle.acb
  have hGEF_HEF : ∠ G E F = ∠ H E F := by
    rw [← hFEH, angle_symm hEF.symm hEHF.ne₁₂.symm]
  -- therefore the base FG is equal to the base FH. [I. 4]
  have hFG_FH : ‖G F‖ = ‖H F‖ := (BookI.Prop4 hEFG.acb hEHF hEH.symm hEF_common hGEF_HEF).1
  have hFH : ‖F H‖ = ‖F G‖ := by rw [len_symm F H, len_symm F G]; exact hFG_FH.symm
  -- I say again that another straight line equal to FG will not fall on the circle from the
  -- point F.
  refine ⟨H, hH, hHG, hFH, ?_⟩
  -- For, if possible, let FK so fall.
  intro K hK hFK
  -- Then, since FK is equal to FG, and FH to FG,
  -- FK is also equal to FH,
  have hFKH : ‖F K‖ = ‖F H‖ := hFK.trans hFH.symm
  -- the nearer to the straight line through the centre being thus equal to the more remote:
  -- which is impossible.
  /- On one side of AD, two points of the circle equally distant from F are one point:
     were they two, one would be the nearer to FA, and greater. -/
  have hone : ∀ X Y : Point, OnCircle X ABCD → OnCircle Y ABCD → SameSideOf X Y A D →
      ‖F X‖ = ‖F Y‖ → X = Y := by
    intro X Y hX hY hXY hFXY
    rcases lt_trichotomy (∠ A F X) (∠ A F Y) with h | h | h
    · exact absurd hFXY (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (hnearer X Y hX hY hXY h)).symm
    · have hXY' : SameSideOf X Y F A :=
        SameSideOf.of_line hFA hF_L hA_L (hXY.sameSide hA_L hD_L)
      exact (onRay_of_angle_eq hXY' h).eq_of_len_eq hFXY
    · exact absurd hFXY (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (hnearer Y X hY hX hXY.symm h))
  by_cases hK_L : OnLine K L
  · /- A point K on the diameter is A, the greatest, or D, the least. -/
    have hGA : G ≠ A := fun e => hG_L (e ▸ hA_L)
    have hGD : G ≠ D := fun e => hG_L (e ▸ hD_L)
    by_cases hKA : K = A
    · subst hKA
      exact absurd hFK (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (hgreatest G hG hGA)).symm
    · have hKD := hends K hK hK_L hKA
      subst hKD
      exact absurd hFK (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (hleast G hG hGD))
  by_cases hKG : SameSideOf K G A D
  · exact Or.inl (hone K G hK hG hKG hFK)
  · have hKG' : OppositeSidesOf K G A D :=
      OppositeSidesOf.of_line hAD hA_L hD_L
        ⟨hK_L, hG_L, fun hs => hKG (SameSideOf.of_line hAD hA_L hD_L hs)⟩
    exact Or.inr (hone K H hK hH (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hKG'.symm hHG.symm)
      hFKH)
  -- Therefore another straight line equal to GF will not fall from the point F upon the
  -- circle;
  -- therefore only one straight line will so fall.
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.
```

**Reading the figure**

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L74) (used here): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L66) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `D` is between `A` and `B`, then `D` is between `A` and `C`. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L70): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `C` is between `B` and `D`, then `B` is between `A` and `D`. (Between 5)
- [`between_of_inside_chord`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L155) (used here): A straight line through a point inside a circle has that point between the points where it meets the circle. (Circle 1)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L43) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, it is between `C` and `A`. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L35) (used here): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L201): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_of_on_inside_outside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L195): Two circles cut one another if the first passes through a point `A` inside the second, and a point `B` outside the second is inside or on the first. (Intersection 4, in LeanEuclid's corrected form)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L81): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L26) (used here): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L38): Let a point be taken between `B` and `C`. (Points 3)
- [`exists_point_opposite_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L46) (used here): Let a point be taken on the other side of `L` from `B`. (Points 6)
- [`inside_not_on`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L38) (used here): A point inside a circle is not on it. (Generalities 4)
- [`inside_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L161) (used here): A circle is "convex": between two points on or inside it, every point is inside. (Circle 2)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L69): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, heading out to a point `C` outside it, cuts the circle between `B` and `C`. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L75) (used here): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, produced beyond `B` away from `C`, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)
- [`line_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L28) (used here): Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1)
- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L179) (used here): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of `L` crosses `L`. (Intersection 1)
- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L46) (used here): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L49) (used here): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L52) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, then `A` is not between `B` and `C`. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L79) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and also between `A` and `D`, then `B` is not between `C` and `D`: `C` and `D` lie on the same side of `B`. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L92) (used here): Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L56) (used here): A straight line through `A` and `B`, with `B` between `A` and `C`, passes through `C`. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L61) (used here): A straight line through `A` and `C` passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, `A` is on `L` and `B` is off it, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `L`: a straight line that leaves `L` at `A` does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114) (used here): A straight line through a point between `A` and `C` separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119) (used here): If two different straight lines `L` and `M` meet at `B`, and `A` and `C` are points of `M`, different from each other and from `B`, that are not on the same side of `L`, then `B` is between `A` and `C`. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99) (used here): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L85) (used here): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L89) (used here): If `A` is on the same side of a straight line as `B`, then `B` is on the same side as `A`. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L96) (used here): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L131) (used here): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`. If `C` lies within the angle `BAD` (on `D`'s side of `L` and on `B`'s side of `N`), then `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`: the straight line `AC` separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139) (used here): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`, with `B` other than `A` and `D` off `M`. If `C` and `D` are on the same side of `L`, and `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `N`: `C` lies within the angle `BAD`. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54) (used here): If `D` lies within the angle `BAC`, then `BAC` is made up of `BAD` and `DAC`. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72) (used here): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle `ABC` is the angle `CBA`. (Metric 4)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `CAB`. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `ACB`. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17) (used here): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21) (used here): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, then `AB` and `BC` together make up `AC`. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23) (used here): The straight line `AB` is the straight line `BA`. (Metric 3)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L49) (used here): If the angle `BAC` is nothing, `C` lies on the ray from `A` through `B`. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle `ABC` can be applied to the straight line `L` with `A` on `D`, `B` on the ray from `D` through `G`, and `C` on the side of `L` where `H` is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (used here): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45) (used here): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (used here): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35) (used here): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39) (used here): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42) (used here): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

**"Only two equal straight lines."** Of the straight lines from F to the circle, FA, through the centre E, is greatest, and FD, the rest of the diameter, is least. Between them Euclid puts everything in order: on either side of AD, the nearer a straight line is to FA, the greater it is, "nearer" meaning the less angle at F. That order does the last part too. Euclid makes FH equal to FG on the other side of AD, and a third would be "the nearer to the straight line through the centre being thus equal to the more remote: which is impossible". So "only two" needs nothing new.

**Nearer at which point?** Augustus De Morgan saw a gap here, and Heath passes it on: "De Morgan points out that there is an unproved assumption in this demonstration" (vol. 2, p. 15). The straight lines are ordered by their angles at F, but I.24 needs the angles at the centre, between equal radii, and Euclid reads off his figure that the angle BEF is greater than CEF. Heath proves it from the crossing of FB and EC, with the perpendicular from E on FB. H. M. Taylor avoids the question by ordering the straight lines by the angle at the centre, but Heath keeps Euclid's plan as "the more instructive and useful of the two" (vol. 2, p. 16).

**The crossing lies within.** We prove De Morgan's step by the circle, in place of Heath's perpendicular. `BookI.Prop24.within` puts FB within the angle EFC, and `crossbar` finds the point where FB crosses EC. That point is between E and C, so it is within the circle (System E, Circle 2), and it comes before B: were B between F and it, B too would be within. So EC falls within the angle BEF, and CEF is less than BEF, just what I.24 needs. Our statement speaks of every point of the circle, and a point of it on AD itself is A or D (System E, Circle 1), the greatest or the least.

**The modern way.** Put E at the origin, let the radius be r, and put F at distance d towards D, with 0 < d < r: a ray making angle θ with FA reaches the circle at distance ρ(θ) = d cos θ + √(r² − d² sin² θ). This strictly decreases from r + d to r − d as θ runs from 0 to π; the symmetry ρ(−θ) = ρ(θ) gives exactly two equal straight lines for every intermediate length, one on each side of AD.

## Further reading

- For the crossbar theorem that closes De Morgan's gap, Marvin Jay Greenberg's [*Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries*](https://store.macmillanlearning.com/us/product/Euclidean-and-Non-Euclidean-Geometries/p/0716799480) (2008), ch. 3, "Hilbert's Axioms", explains the rules of order behind the crossing of FB and EC.
- For how these comparisons fit into the geometry of the circle, Benno Artmann's [*Euclid: The Creation of Mathematics*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-1412-0) (1999), the chapter "Euclid Book III: About the Circle", reads Euclid's arguments with a modern mathematician's eye.
